newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: N. Korean envoy pays courtesy call on Annan.
newsitem.headline: N. Korean envoy pays courtesy call on Annan.

text.p: North Korean U.N. envoy Kim Hyong U paid his first courtesy call on Friday on Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
In reply to a question, he told Reuters they did not discuss the case of Hwang Jang-yop, a high-ranking North Korean official who has sought asylum in South Korea's embassy in Beijing.
"I am sure that this is not an issue to be discussed between myself and the secretary-general of the United Nations," Kim said, speaking through an interpreter.

"We are very sure that this kind of case of so-called political asylum on the part of the secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea's central committee...cannot be conceived of, nor can it happen. We are sure.
"This is nothing but (one of) the historical kidnapping cases pursued by the South Korean authorities," he added.
Kim said he had called on the secretary-general, who took office on Jan. 1, to congratulate him on his appointment and wish him success.
He also expressed gratitude for the recent launching by a U.N. agency of an appeal for assistance to North Korea "with regard to the natural disasters."
He was referring to a $41.5 million appeal by the World Food Programme to avert the danger of famine due to poor harvests and serious flooding.
The North Korean envoy said he told Annan he was sure measures would be taken to ensure that the "abnormal relationship existing between my country and the United Nations" would be rectified.
By this he said he meant what happened after "the United States...started the Korean War in the name of the United Nations and under the flag of the United Nations."
North Korea and the United Nations were then "in a state of war," requiring the removal of obstacles dating from that period.
But he stressed that his meeting with Annan was "not because there is any serious case to discuss with him" but to congratulate him.
